changes: Carried-over hours: Justin entries ticked Roll over now go into a carried-over balance instead of being charged automatically the next month. Hours brought in from Settings join the same balance.
On any later HTB timesheet, the carried-over box shows the balance with buttons: Fill spare weeks, +15m, +30m, +1h, Add all, −15m and Clear. Whatever you don't add stays for later.
Fill spare weeks adds as much as fits in the weeks where Justin was under that week's max. Added hours appear as one invoice line per week, and week totals show '+ carried over'.
Anything you rolled over before this update is now in the balance, ready to add with the buttons.

By-the-week timesheets (e.g. FCY) have an 'Even out the weeks' tick box in Invoice lines. It spreads the month's total evenly over its weeks in whole blocks, with the same total; any spare block goes to the busiest week.
Each smoothed line shows the real hours underneath. The timesheet itself still shows the real week totals. Your choice is remembered for each client.

New Save PDF button on every timesheet (and on the Timesheets tab). The tracker writes the PDF itself and it goes straight to your Downloads folder, with no print box, so Safari can't save a blank page.
The PDF has A4 pages with the same entries, day and week totals, crossed-out excluded entries, adjusted, added and rolled-over notes, the allowance line, and page numbers.
The old print button is now just 'Print'.
Simpler allowances: tick Roll over beside any Justin entry on the timesheet to charge it next month instead.
Rolled entries appear under 'Brought forward' at the top of next month's timesheet and in its invoice lines, where you can roll them on again.
The line at the top of the timesheet shows Justin's maximum for the month, what you're charging, what's rolling over, and whether you're over.
Week totals show Justin's hours against that week's maximum.
The week-by-week table, the Charged boxes and the Charge / Roll over buttons have been removed.
Allowance table: a 'Charged (h)' box on each week and on the brought-forward row. It shows a suggestion; type what you actually charged to replace it, or clear it to go back.
What carries into next month is the hours worked minus the hours you charged.
Charging more than was worked leaves a credit, which next month's hours use up before anything more is charged.
Charging less in one week leaves room in the allowance for later weeks that month.
The table stays open after you change something.
Allowances are now part of Limits: tick 'Bill as allowance' on a task's weekly limit, then choose the month it starts from and any hours brought in. Your existing allowance has moved across.
Limits now have a full-width box in Settings.
The allowance box on the timesheet opens into a week-by-week table showing each week's maximum, Justin's hours, over or under, and the running balance.
Spare hours in a quiet week still take up a busy week's extra hours. For a week that's over, choose Roll over (the default) or Charge to bill that week's extra hours this month.
Printed timesheets show the table with your choices, without the buttons.

Monthly allowances (Settings): cap a task, such as Justin, at so many hours a week. Each month's allowance is the weekly hours shared across its working days, so a week split across two months is shared by its weekdays.
England and Wales bank holidays (downloaded from gov.uk) don't count as working days.
Hours over a month's allowance carry into the next month with room. The timesheet notes them, and the invoice lines include a 'brought forward' line.
You can enter hours brought in from before the allowance starts.
HTB timesheets show a total for each week, with Justin's hours that week.
The dashboard shows this month's allowance: hours used, hours left, and anything carrying over.
New design: a dashboard of small tiles instead of full-width sections, with tabs for Dashboard, Reports, Timesheets and Settings.
Today tile shows your hours, a strip of when you worked (with a marker for now), money earned and own-business value.
Earned today, this week and this month tiles each show progress to their target, plus hours this week.
This week chart: hours per day, coloured by client. Targets and limits sit together in one tile.
This month shows one card per client; monthly income is entered on its card.
Targets: set income targets per day, week and month, and time targets per client (e.g. FYPTD hours per week) in Settings. Progress shows in a new Targets section.
Income targets count real money only. FYPT1 counts as an estimate from last month (its income, and its per-hour rate for days and weeks) until you enter the month's actual income.
The daily target is weekdays only unless you tick “Daily target on weekends too”; weekend earnings still show.
Fixed: saving limits or “Tasks not counted” no longer clears hourly rates you've typed but not yet saved.
The invoicing settings now say “Unsaved changes” until you click Save invoicing settings.
Settings → Tasks not counted: tick sides such as breaks, timers or “off” to leave them out of Today, charts, limits, This month and timesheets.
Today shows how much time wasn't counted.
New This month section: hours, money and per-hour rate for each client.
Set a client (e.g. FYPT1) to “Monthly income” in Settings, enter what it brings in, and see your effective hourly rate. The amount carries forward to later months until you change it.
Today now shows money earned from paying clients, using the hourly rates in Settings and the same rounding as your invoices.
Tick “My own business” beside a client (e.g. FYPT1, FYPTD) to give its time an imagined rate. It shows separately as own-business value and never appears on timesheets.
“Where your time went” shows the value of each client or task, with earned and own-business totals.
New Today section at the top: your total for today, time per task, and today's entries.
The settings tables now scroll sideways in a narrow window instead of spilling off the page.
Edit any entry on a timesheet: change its date, start and end times, or move it to a different task or client.
Add entries for time you didn't track on the cube, with + Add entry at the top of a timesheet.
Adjusted entries are marked “adjusted” with the original time, and added ones “added”, including on printed sheets. Back to original undoes an edit.
TimeFlip Tracker now has its own app with an orange clock icon, in your Applications folder. Open it from Launchpad or Spotlight, or drag it into your Dock.
Settings shows where the app is, with a Show in Finder button.
New look in Future You PT colours and fonts: dark header bar, orange accents, Sora headings.
Timesheets and invoice lines use the same colours.
Monthly timesheets now have an Invoice lines panel: one line per day (HTB) or per week (FCY), with Copy buttons for pasting into a Revolut Business invoice.
You can set an hourly rate for each client in Settings → How each client is invoiced, to show amounts on the invoice lines.
Updates now install automatically overnight (you can switch this off in Settings).
A “What's new” message like this one appears after each update.
Update now button, so new versions install without downloading a ZIP.
Your version number is shown in Settings, with a Check for updates button.
Monthly timesheets for clients billed by the day (HTB) or by the week (FCY), with day and week totals.
Exclude any entry you won't charge for. It stays on the sheet, crossed out, and isn't counted.
Each day's total can be rounded to 15-minute blocks.
